full_judgment:
3. The petitioners herein as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.572 of 1970 in the First Court of the then Munsif Kushtia for declaration of title. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit property measuring 18.15 acres recorded under C. S. khatian No. 622 of Kazihatta mouza originally belonged to Brojendra Nath Chattpadhya who passed away leaving behind three sons, Jitendra Nath, Upendra Nath and  Gopal Chattapdhya. After that, Upendra Nath passed away leaving behind three sons, Dhirendra Nath, Sailendra Nath and Hirandra Nath Chattpadhya. While the co-sharers were in possession of the suit land, Jitendra Nath settled the suit land with plaintiff Nos.1-2 with the consent of all other co-sharers on 15th Chaitra, 1357 B.S. at a jama of Rs.30 annas 6 on the basis of dakhila. At that time, the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land and they got there names correctly recorded during rent roll operation. Subsequently, the plaintiffs came to know that defendant No.1 managed to pay rent of the suit land for three years from 1371 B.S. with the help of Tahsilder by manipulating and inserting his name in the tenants ledger. The plaintiffs further came to know that the relevant Khatian had been removed and replaced by a new khatian at the instance of defendant No. 1. Defendant No.1 had no right, title and possession in the suit land. The record standing in the name of defendant No.1 had cast cloud I upon the plaintiffs' title to the suit land. Consequently, the plaintiffs were constrained   to file this suit for declaration of their title. 

 4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material   statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that he purchased 26.76 acres of land including the suit land from Brojendra Nath by a registered deed dated 08.07.1946. After acquisition of the suit land, he had been possessing the same by paying rent to the ex-landlord and the then to the Government. Part of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the plaintiff’s husband. One Tarapada filed a suit for rectification of the record in respect of the suit land and the plaintiffs being aware about the suit filed another suit with a view to harassing the defendant and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the leave petitioners, submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court without taking into consideration the fact that defendant No.1 could not prove his title to the suit land measuring an area of 26.76 acres and that without reversing the judgment of the trial Court as regards the title of the plaintiffs to the spit land dismissed the second appeal by the impugned judgment and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that having taken into consideration the rent receipts, the High Court Division came to a finding that those could not be proved in accordance with law although the plaintiffs' witnesses could prove those rent receipts in accordance   with law and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division while concurring with the judgment of the appellate Court came to a finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land without reversing the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their possession in the suit land and as such, the impugned judgment cannot sustain in law.
